actionable_lessons: Ask questions instead of giving direct orders.
Questions invite participation and preserve autonomy; orders often provoke silent resistance.
arguments: If he had asked in a friendly way, “Whose car is in the driveway?” and then suggested that if it were moved, other cars could get in and out, the student would have gladly moved it and neither he nor his classmates would have been upset and resentful.
definitions: Principle: Ask questions instead of giving direct orders.

key_points: When I told her I was writing this book, we began discussing this all-important subject of getting along with people, and she told me that while she was writing her biography of Owen D.
A technique like that saves a person’s pride and gives him or her a feeling of importance.

If he had asked in a friendly way, “Whose car is in the driveway?” and then suggested that if it were moved, other cars could get in and out, the student would have gladly moved it and neither he nor his classmates would have been upset and resentful.
Asking questions not only makes an order more palatable; it often stimulates the creativity of the persons whom you ask.
PRINCIPLE 4 Ask questions instead of giving direct orders.
